name: Sena
notes: Sena (Chisena/Cisena, Nuclear Sena, Guthrie N.44), Bantu language spoken along the lower Zambezi valley in Mozambique (Sofala/Zambezia provinces) and adjoining Malawi. Five vowel qualities a/e/i/o/u. Rich affricate and aspirate inventory: plain vs aspirated stops (p/ph, t/th, k/kh) and a series of affricates (bv, ps, pf, dz, ts, tsh, ch). Implosives [ɓ, ɗ] occur as allophones of /b, d/ in some varieties. Labialized sibilants sw/zw (/sʷ, zʷ/) may surface as retroflex [ʂ, ʐ]. ⟨ng'⟩ marks the bare velar nasal /ŋ/. Prenasalized consonants occur after homorganic nasal noun-class prefixes but are not written as fixed digraphs the way Nguni/Nyanja mb/nd are, since the nasal is a separate morpheme; the language is tonal, unmarked in the standard orthography.

sources.author: Ngunga, Armindo

sources.notes: Comparative Bantu reference used for the region's phonological conventions (Sena, Yao).

ancestors.notes: Sena branch of Bantu (Guthrie N.40), within Atlantic-Congo.

location.notes: Approximate centre of the lower Zambezi valley Sena-speaking area, Mozambique.
